purpose: freeze the minimum proof artifacts for route-first ChatGPT claims so screenshots, retrying assertions, traces, and auth posture stay distinct instead of being flattened into one vague “we have proof” sentence

source_refs.title: The ChatGPT home page
source_refs.notes: Current first-party help anchor for the direct browser home route at chatgpt.com and its pre-login posture.

source_refs.title: Best Practices
source_refs.notes: Best Practices says tests should verify user-visible behavior and remain isolated with separate local/session storage and cookies for reproducibility.

source_refs.title: Assertions
source_refs.notes: Assertions docs emphasize async web assertions like toHaveText/toHaveValue that re-fetch until UI state settles instead of one-shot DOM reads.

source_refs.title: Authentication
source_refs.notes: Authentication docs say tests run in isolated browser contexts, can reuse saved auth state, and should keep playwright/.auth out of git because state files may contain sensitive cookies and headers.

source_refs.title: Trace viewer
source_refs.notes: Trace Viewer docs say recorded traces can be opened after the run and inspected for action timeline, DOM snapshots, console messages, and network requests, which makes traces stronger evidence than a screenshot alone.

source_refs.title: Screenshots
source_refs.notes: Screenshots docs describe capturing page screenshots, including full-page captures, so route/composer/latest-turn proof can preserve a rendered visual snapshot instead of only a text transcript.

artifact_catalog.label: First-party route/source anchor
artifact_catalog.artifact_shape: cite the current first-party ChatGPT route or feature page that defines the surface being discussed
artifact_catalog.why_it_exists: A proof sentence needs a named official surface anchor before screenshots or selectors can mean anything.

artifact_catalog.label: Rendered screenshot
artifact_catalog.artifact_shape: capture a visible screenshot of the routed page state, composer state, or latest-turn state being claimed
artifact_catalog.why_it_exists: A screenshot preserves what the operator actually saw instead of leaving the proof as only prose or a DOM transcript.

artifact_catalog.label: Retrying visible-state assertion
artifact_catalog.artifact_shape: record a retrying Playwright web assertion against visible UI state such as value, text, or visibility
artifact_catalog.why_it_exists: ChatGPT proof should survive streaming and rerender timing rather than depending on one-shot reads.

artifact_catalog.label: Replayable trace bundle
artifact_catalog.artifact_shape: capture a Playwright trace so the action timeline, DOM snapshots, network requests, and console output can be reviewed after the run
artifact_catalog.why_it_exists: Traces preserve post-run replay context that a screenshot alone cannot carry.

artifact_catalog.label: Auth and storage-state note
artifact_catalog.artifact_shape: record whether the proof used logged-out state, fresh login, or isolated reused auth state, and keep sensitive state files out of the repo
artifact_catalog.why_it_exists: The same screenshot or assertion can mean different things in guest, personal, or managed workspace contexts.

evidence_ladder.why: Planning can stay source-backed, but it should not claim that a live rendered browser flow was captured.
An investigated claim should show a named official route, a visible rendered state, a retrying UI assertion, and the auth posture used for the run.
Once wording starts leaning on stronger live proof, the bundle should be replayable rather than relying on screenshots and prose alone.

proof_windows.safe_bundle_sentence: A route-first ChatGPT landing proof should cite the current chatgpt.com home-route page, preserve a screenshot of the landed browser state, and record whether the run was logged out or used isolated reused auth state.

A composer-write proof should preserve the rendered textbox state in a screenshot, verify the typed probe text with a retrying UI assertion, and record the auth/storage-state posture used for that write.

A latest-turn proof should preserve the rendered assistant state with a screenshot, confirm visible text with a retrying assertion, and keep a trace bundle so streaming timing, network, and DOM snapshots remain reviewable after the run.

review_checks: Does the claim cite the current first-party ChatGPT route or feature page it is talking about?
Does the proof preserve at least one rendered screenshot of the claimed page state?
Does the proof use a retrying visible-state assertion instead of a one-shot DOM read?
Does stronger live proof include a replayable trace bundle rather than only screenshots?
Does the bundle record whether it was logged out, freshly logged in, or using isolated reused auth state?
